Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part I: the two digit current tax year
Fact.Description: The two digits the Part I release prints after the printed 20, which for this dictionary's tax year is 25. A constant, not an intake: Part I releases the current year and this is a TY2025 dictionary.

Fact.Name: The custodial parent is completing a Form 8332 release or revocation
Fact.Description: Whether the custodial parent is completing a Form 8332 release (Part I/II) or revocation (Part III) with this return's information. It is the return-level election that a Form 8332 is being completed at all, not itself the render gate: the printed population is the per-child collection /form8332Children, which pairs this election with the child-level release or revocation signal. A Part I/II release is signed by the custodial parent and given to the noncustodial parent, who attaches it to THEIR return (see familyAndHousehold:/familyAndHousehold/*/writableNoncustodialParentHasReleaseToAttach's Description) — but this return's printed package is the only place the custodial parent can obtain the copy to sign, so the copy is printed here. Nothing in the graph implies the election, because a release or revocation is a document the custodial parent chooses to sign.

Fact.Name: This return attaches a Form 8332 Part III revocation copy
Fact.Description: Whether the custodial parent's own return attaches at least one Form 8332 Part III revocation copy. Part III is the only Part the custodial parent files with their own return: "You must attach a copy of the revocation to your tax return each year the exemption is claimed as a result of the revocation." A Part I/II release is instead signed and handed to the noncustodial parent, who attaches it to THEIR return; this return's printed package still carries the copy, because that package is the only place the filer can obtain the form to sign, but it is not an attachment to this return. This fact is the return-level "at least one" summary of /form8332RevokedChildren. It is NOT the render gate: dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv's IRS8332 row renders one copy per child in /form8332Children, the released and the revoked children together.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part III: this child's release is being revoked
Fact.Description:
Whether the custodial parent is revoking an earlier release of claim to exemption for THIS child (drawn from the household collection, not re-asked). Form 8332 is filed once per child ("Attach a separate form for each child"), so this is asked once per household member rather than once per return.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION - the application implements this without opening a statute.
QUESTION TEXT, with the child's name substituted for {name}: "Are you revoking an earlier release of your claim to {name} as a dependent?"
HELP TEXT: "Use Part III of Form 8332 to revoke a release you signed earlier for this child. The revocation takes effect no earlier than the year after you give the noncustodial parent a copy, and you must attach a copy of this form to your own return each year you claim the exemption as a result of the revocation." Source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8332.pdf, page 1 and lines 44-77 (Revocation of release of claim to exemption, and the Custodial Parent attachment duty).
ASKED WHEN: /writableForm8332FilesReleaseOrRevocation is true, once per /familyAndHousehold member the custodial parent identifies as a child of a released earlier declaration.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: unanswered means NOT revoked — a silent household member prints no copy and is not counted in /form8332RevokedChildren. No Placeholder, no default value beyond that safe reading.
VALIDATION: Boolean. Yes/No radio, no default selection, answer required to leave the screen. No Min/Max.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../form8332PartIIIRevokedCompleteSafe -> /form8332RevokedChildren and, unioned with the released children, /form8332Children (the `includeForEach` render gate, dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv) -> one Form 8332 copy for this child, carrying this child's name (../form8332PartIIIChildName) and ../writableForm8332PartIIIRevocationTaxYears on the Part III lines.

Fact.Name: This child's Part III revocation is in effect (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: The complete-safe reading of ../writableForm8332PartIIIRevoked: an unanswered household member resolves Complete false, so /form8332RevokedChildren never grows on silence and the render gate never fires on an incomplete intake.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part III: the tax years this child's revocation covers
Fact.Description:
The tax years this child's Part III revocation covers, which the printed line asks the filer to specify. Per child, not per return, because a parent revoking for two children can specify different years for each.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION - the application implements this without opening a statute.
QUESTION TEXT, with the child's name substituted for {name}: "Which tax year or years are you revoking the release for {name}?"
HELP TEXT: "Form 8332 asks you to write the year or years the revocation covers. A revocation cannot take effect before the tax year AFTER the year you give the noncustodial parent a copy of it (or make a reasonable effort to). So if you give them the copy in 2025, the earliest year you can revoke is 2026. You can name a single year, a list of years, or a phrase such as 'all future years'." Source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8332.pdf, page 1 (Use Part III to revoke a previous release; the revocation is effective no earlier than the tax year following the year the copy is provided) and lines 37-38 (the printed line, "for the tax year(s) ... Specify").
ASKED WHEN: ../writableForm8332PartIIIRevoked is true for this household member. Not asked of a member with no revocation, and never asked once per return: it belongs to the child's own copy of the form.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the printed form. The field is free text the filer writes on the paper form, so silence prints nothing rather than a guess, and it does NOT suppress the copy: /form8332Children is gated on the revocation answer, not on this one, so a filer who revokes but leaves the years blank still gets a form to complete by hand. No Placeholder and no default.
VALIDATION: String, free text, no Min/Max and no enum. Not parsed into years anywhere in the dictionary; it is transcribed onto the form as typed.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: the Part III "for the tax year(s)" line of this child's copy, f1_10 in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8332/en/configuration.yml, reached as /form8332Children/*/writableForm8332PartIIIRevocationTaxYears.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part III: children whose release is being revoked
Fact.Description: The household members for whom the custodial parent completes a Part III revocation. This is the Part III half of /form8332Children, the printed population, and is what /form8332RevokedChildrenCount and /form8332AttachesPartIIIRevocation measure — the subset whose copies the custodial parent also attaches to this return. An empty collection is the no-revocation return.

Fact.Name: Count of children whose Form 8332 release is being revoked
Fact.Description: The size of /form8332RevokedChildren — how many Part III copies this render surface prints. Zero on the no-revocation return.

Fact.Name: The return is completing a Form 8332 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: The complete-safe reading of /writableForm8332FilesReleaseOrRevocation: an unanswered election resolves Complete false, so no child joins /form8332Children until the filer says a Form 8332 is being completed. It is what keeps a child whose claim was released by a pre-1985 or post-1984 divorce decree, with no Form 8332 completed at all, out of the printed population.

Fact.Name: This child's claim is released on a Form 8332 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Whether a filer on this return signs a Form 8332 Part I/II release of the claim to THIS child. Read from the benefit-split answer already asked rather than re-asked: dependentsBenefitSplit's ../primaryFilerNotClaiming and ../bothFilersNotClaiming are the two derived readings of ../whichParentNotClaiming = "iDid" ("I signed the written declaration not to claim this child"), one for a return not treated as joint and one for a joint return, so their disjunction is exactly the released population. Complete-safe in both directions: both readings depend on filingStatus:/treatAsMFJ and are Incomplete until the filing status is settled, so their completeness is tested before they are read and an unanswered child reads false. The return-level /form8332FilesReleaseOrRevocationCompleteSafe conjunct keeps a release made by decree rather than on a Form 8332 out of the printed population.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part III: the child name printed on this child's copy
Fact.Description: The name printed on the Part III line "I revoke the release of claim to an exemption for" of THIS child's copy: this household member's own ../fullName when the copy carries a revocation, and blank otherwise. The blank branch is load-bearing — /form8332Children also renders a copy for a child whose claim is being RELEASED, and Part III of that copy states a revocation nobody made, so it must print empty.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part I: the child name printed on this child's copy
Fact.Description: The name printed on the Part I line "I agree not to claim an exemption for" of THIS child's copy: this household member's own ../fullName when a filer on this return releases the claim to this child for the current year (../form8332ReleaseSignedCompleteSafe, read from the "I signed the written declaration not to claim this child" answer), and blank otherwise, since Part I of a copy for a revocation-only or future-years-only child states a release nobody made. One form per child, so each copy names its own child.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part II: the future tax years released for this child
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Are you also releasing your claim to this child for future years? If so, which years? (for example, 2026 and 2027, or all future years)". Asked when the return completes a Form 8332 (/writableForm8332FilesReleaseOrRevocation) for this household member. Free text, as the printed Part II line asks the filer to specify the years. Unanswered means no Part II release for this child: Part II of this child's copy prints blank. Each child has its own Form 8332, so the answer is per child.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 Part II: the child name printed on this child's copy
Fact.Description: The name printed on the Part II line of THIS child's copy: this household member's own ../fullName when the Part II future years are answered for this child (../writableForm8332PartIIReleaseTaxYears), and blank otherwise.

Fact.Name: A Form 8332 goes with this return, so an e-filed return sends it with Form 8453
Fact.Description: True when this return carries a Form 8332 as an attachment: the custodial parent's own Part III revocation copy (/form8332AttachesPartIIIRevocation), or, on the noncustodial parent's return, a signed release the filer has in hand for a child (dependentsBenefitSplit:/familyAndHousehold/*/noncustodialParentHasReleaseToAttach). Form 8332 says that a return filed electronically files Form 8332 with Form 8453, the U.S. Individual Income Tax Transmittal for an IRS e-file Return, whose attachment list names Form 8332 (and the post-1984, pre-2009 decree pages that may stand in for it). This is the fact the e-file transmittal reads to check that Form 8453 box; a paper return attaches the form directly. Complete-safe false when neither is answered.

Fact.Name: Children this return prints a Form 8332 for
Fact.Description: The household members this return prints a Form 8332 copy for — the render population of dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv's IRS8332 row (`includeForEach`). It is the UNION of the children whose claim a filer releases for the current year (Part I) or for future years (Part II, ../writableForm8332PartIIReleaseTaxYears answered) and the children whose earlier release a filer revokes (Part III), because the form header says "Attach a separate form for each child": one copy per child, carrying whichever Parts that child needs. Release and revocation are not two render populations, they are two Parts of one form. A release is not an attachment to this return — the custodial parent signs it and hands it to the noncustodial parent, who attaches it to theirs — but this return's printed package is the only place the filer can obtain the copy to sign, so the copy is printed here. An empty collection is the return that files no Form 8332.

Fact.Name: Count of children this return prints a Form 8332 for
Fact.Description: The size of /form8332Children — how many Form 8332 copies this render surface prints. Zero on a return that files none.

Fact.Name: Form 8332: the custodial parent signing is the secondary filer
Fact.Description:
Whether the custodial parent releasing or revoking the claim is the SECONDARY filer on this joint return, asked only when the return is married filing jointly. Every "Custodial parent's SSN" box on the form belongs to whichever parent actually signs that Part, and on an MFJ return the two filers are not interchangeable: a remarried custodial parent can be listed second, with the primary filer being the new spouse who is not a party to the release at all.
QUESTION TEXT, as asked: "Are you the second person listed on this joint return (not the first person named on Form 1040)?" asked once, in the Form 8332 section, immediately after the return confirms it is filing a release or revocation.
HELP TEXT: "Form 8332 asks for the Social Security number of the parent releasing or revoking the claim. On a joint return we need to know which of you that is, so the right SSN prints next to the signature."
ASKED WHEN: /writableForm8332FilesReleaseOrRevocation is true AND the return's filing status is married filing jointly. Not asked on any other filing status, because there is only one filer to sign.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: unanswered means primary filer signs. The custodial parent is who opens this section of the interview, and on every return that has reached this screen before it existed the primary filer was the (only) signer, so silence must not move the SSN off the primary filer's box; the wrong-but-narrower defect this fact fixes is the REMARRIED-secondary-signs case that requires an affirmative Yes.
VALIDATION: Boolean. Yes/No radio, no default selection when asked, answer required to leave the screen. No Min/Max.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /form8332SigningFilerTin, which is the fact printed in every "Custodial parent's SSN" box on the rendered form (f1_5, f1_8, f1_11 in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8332/en/configuration.yml).

Fact.Name: Form 8332 signer is the secondary filer (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: The complete-safe reading of /writableForm8332SignerIsSecondaryFiler: an unanswered or not-yet-reached screen resolves Complete false, so /form8332SigningFilerTin always completes to the primary filer's TIN until an MFJ filer affirmatively says the secondary filer is the one signing. Not gated on filing status here — a non-MFJ return simply never has this writable answered, and false is the correct reading of that silence too.
The primary filer used by Form 8332 signing-TIN selection
The secondary filer used by Form 8332 signing-TIN selection

Fact.Name: Form 8332: the signing custodial parent's SSN
Fact.Description: The SSN printed in every "Custodial parent's SSN" box on the rendered form — the secondary filer's TIN when /form8332SignerIsSecondaryFilerCompleteSafe is true, otherwise the primary filer's TIN. On an MFJ return where the remarried custodial parent is the secondary filer, only that filer's SSN belongs beside the signature, since only the custodial parent under IRC 152(e)(2)(A) can sign the release.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 header: name of the noncustodial parent
Fact.Description: The name of the noncustodial parent the custodial parent releases the claim to. The other parent is not a person this dictionary holds: /filers is the return's own filers and /familyAndHousehold is the household, neither of which carries a parent who lives elsewhere. So the name is the filer's own entry.

Fact.Name: Form 8332 header: social security number of the noncustodial parent
Fact.Description: The noncustodial parent's social security number, the second identity box of the header. Like the name beside it, it names a person outside the return and is the filer's own entry.
